summary: Account egress path flip after partner BGP advertisement causing sustained p95 inference latency spike
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth reported a sudden increase in p95 generation latency and periodic streaming timeouts for API requests originating from APAC users around 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC. The spike lasted ~90 minutes for affected accounts and coincided with an external partner maintenance window.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints for AtlasHealth saw p95 rise from ~220ms to 1400-2500ms.
- Streaming sessions experienced 5-10% session resets and delayed first-byte for responses.
- Customer-facing alerts: users reported slow response times and occasional 'stream disconnected' errors.

Environment:
- Prod edge PoPs: apac-southeast-1 edge POPs; backend model serving in eu-west-1 dedicated cluster for AtlasHealth.
- Affected account uses routing tag "account:atlas-prod" with egress affinity enabled.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a batch of streaming chat requests to the customer's pinned model endpoint from an APAC client (sequence length ~512).
2) Repeat until 10k tokens processed or until p95 >= 1000ms observed.
3) Capture tcpdump on edge-proxy and record request_id headers.

Observed:
- Elevated retransmits and increased TCP RTT between APAC edge and eu-west backend causing delayed TCP handshake completion and delayed first byte.
- Edge traces show route went via a remote transit partner POP (us-west-2 transit path) instead of direct regional backbone.
- KV/prefix cache hit rate dropped for affected account due to traffic being steered to a different serving pool, causing cold cache penalties.

Expected:
- Traffic from APAC edge should take shortest backbone path to eu-west serving pool with low retransmit rate and stable RTT < 300ms.

Relevant artifacts (trace ids / logs):
- Example request_id: req_20260310_amoX92 (tcpdump capture attached to ticket).
- Edge trace: edge-trace-apac-20260310-09:45 (link in related_confluence_pages).
- Partner maintenance notice: transit-partner-postmortem-20260310 (external link).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:55 UTC — Aisha Kapoor: Customer reported spike via support channel. Initial triage shows p95 increase across multiple routes. Opening incident and paging network on-call.

2026-03-10 10:05 UTC — Diego Martinez (SRE): Correlated increased TCP retransmits from apac edge -> eu-west. Noting partner transit AS path changed at 09:38 UTC. Escalating to network infra and contacting partner NOC.

2026-03-10 10:40 UTC — Network Infra (Liu Chen): Partner acknowledged a misconfigured BGP community during planned change; they withdrew and re-advertised prefixes causing some accounts to be attracted to remote POPs. Asking partner to rollback specific community for our account prefixes.

2026-03-10 11:15 UTC — Diego Martinez: As a mitigation applied account routing pin: forced egress via our APAC backbone (routing override) for atlas-prod. Observed p95 drop to ~300ms for retested flows. Instructed customer to retry streaming sessions.

2026-03-10 13:05 UTC — Partner NOC: Confirmed rollback of the problematic advertisement at 10:55 UTC; BGP table stabilized by 11:05 UTC. Partner to add validation to prevent community leak in future changes.
2026-03-12 08:30 UTC — Support Manager (Rhea Patel): Closing the ticket after post-incident verification with customer. Will follow up with permanent mitigations and a short postmortem summary.
2026-03-12 09:00 UTC — AtlasHealth (John Simmons): Confirming that performance returned to normal and no further customer-impacting errors observed. Appreciated quick mitigation actions.
investigation_notes: Collected tcpdump (edge-proxy apac-southeast-1) for req_20260310_amoX92: observed threefold increase in duplicate ACKs and retransmits during spike window.

BGP routing delta: our account-prefixed /24s were tagged with partner-community 65010:500 which caused traffic-steering to partner PoP in us-west-2. This introduced an extra transit hop and increased packet loss.
Serving runtime logs indicate KV cache miss rate for atlas-prod increased from 7% baseline to 44% during the period — likely due to session affinity flip to a different serving cluster.
No changes on our side to autoscaling or rollout configs at time of incident. Canary deployment windows checked and clear.
Hypothesis: external BGP community misconfiguration caused asymmetric path and remote egress, increasing RTT and introducing packet loss -> TCP stalls -> higher p95 and streaming resets.
Cross-checked with partner maintenance window and BGP updates observed in our collectors: exact timestamp alignment with the customer impact window.
Ran targeted repro after routing override: p95 returned close to baseline and retransmit metrics normalized, which supports routing hypothesis.
Scheduled deeper post-incident network trace with partner; requested full BGP update dump and community-tag audit.
Related runbook: applied temporary routing override per 'Egress path pinning' section in BGP Egress Runbook.
root_cause: External transit partner inadvertently advertised our account prefixes with a BGP community that steered egress to a remote PoP. This caused asymmetric, longer transit with elevated packet loss and cold-serving-cluster hits for the affected account.
resolution:
Short-term: Applied account-level egress override (routing pin) to force traffic over our APAC backbone and restored expected path for atlas-prod. Partner rolled back the misadvertisement; global BGP tables converged and retransmit rates returned to baseline.

Long-term actions: partner committed to community validation checks on deploys; we added an automated detection alert for sudden account-level AS path changes and a playbook item to auto-apply egress pin when retransmits and p95 exceed thresholds for a single account.

Customer communication: Notified AtlasHealth of cause, mitigation steps, and planned preventative measures. Customer validated recovery and accepted ticket closure.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add automated detection for account-level AS path flips with alerting to network-oncall (owner: Network Infra).
2) Implement safe-guard in egress routing controller to reject route advertisements that unexpectedly change community tags for pinned accounts (owner: Routing Team).
3) Update BGP Egress Runbook with additional verification steps for partners and include a rollback checklist (owner: SRE).
4) Coordinate a joint drill with transit partner to validate their community-tag validation process (owner: Partnerships).
